limitations: Live scope is Q3; other profiles have shared source/affected tests only.
Synthetic BODY motion does not establish every retail player animation.
Input intervals are CPU/API measurements, not input-to-photon latency.
Other game sessions used the GPU during parts of timing comparisons.
The local x86 driver exposes no required KHR hardware tracing; x64 Q3 is diagnostic only.
No universal spawn generation exists in identity-free external entity contracts.
GPU skinning remains an evaluated follow-up; compute BVHs still need CPU poses.
Proposal replay is implemented and energy-tested but remains opt-in due unproven noise benefit.
Independent indirect density does not reduce full-resolution intermediate storage.
No complete profile, Linux runtime or broad GPU-driver gate is closed.
unrelatedIssues: Q3-only x64 all target includes x86-only JKA ABI tests and fails their layout assertions; targeted Q3 client/RTX build passes.

fixture.note: Existing additional paks are present; not untouched-retail image parity.

audit.finding: A static receiver keeps a moving entity's shadow in long history.
audit.disposition: Direct, indirect and specular histories are separate. Dynamic shadow blockers, including BODY, mark direct illumination reactive for 150 ms; reactive direct response is 35 ms, static direct 320 ms, specular 60 ms and indirect 160 ms. Response uses elapsed time. Executed shader math covers 20, 60, 120 and 240 FPS; consecutive engine captures move the shadow on every frame.

audit.finding: History-derived firefly clipping suppresses light when an entity uncovers it.
audit.disposition: Compatible current-neighbourhood bounds clip old history instead of capping new light to old darkness. Frozen accumulation remains a running average; indirect variance includes sample residual and effective sample count. Pulse, dark-to-light, outlier and frozen-mean tests execute the actual helper math.

audit.finding: An RTX-branded GPU does not establish the active tracing backend.
audit.disposition: Startup/capability and timing reports name compute or hardware. Compute defaults to indirect divisor 2, hardware to 1. An optional measured GPU budget adjusts indirect density with hysteresis. The local Win32 driver exposes no required KHR ray-tracing capability; the Q3-only x64 probe runs the hardware path. See the architecture finding below.

Optional internal renderer API 35 frame events move fence waits and presentation acquisition before OS input polling. Default `rtx_rt_low_latency 1` limits GPU work to one frame in flight; 2 allows two, 0 restores late waits. Monotonic input/simulation/submit/present events and rolling CPU/GPU p50/p95/p99 distinguish frame cost from wait placement. No queue-idle workaround or game-clock change is introduced.

audit.finding: Full raster shading is discarded under the traced image.
audit.disposition: Trace-owned base surfaces write depth only. Opaque surfaces use position-only depth; cutouts retain authored alpha coverage and EQUAL-depth dependencies. Raster shadow maps are scheduled from their remaining consumers, retaining all required casters. A permissive trace failure clears the partial base and redraws complete raster colour, lighting, shadows and fog. Executed coverage tests and compute/hardware failure/recovery captures pass.

audit.finding: Dynamic geometry and acceleration structures are rebuilt needlessly.
audit.disposition: A bounded, exact-pose model-space cache handles MD3/MDR/IQM/brush models; current transforms, lighting and motion are applied each frame. IQM scratch is reused. Compute BVHs refit exact connectivity with cost/age rebuild thresholds; hardware BLASes UPDATE stable topology with periodic rebuilding. Cache tests include tiny interpolation changes, transforms, material changes, eviction, invalidation and allocation failure. No animation quantization or caster throttling is used.

audit.finding: Nearest matching can swap histories between identical models.
audit.disposition: Internal entity IDs where supplied by RTCW/ET, model/part topology, material generation and one-to-one matching replace proximity-only reuse. Ambiguous identity-free duplicates, changed topology/materials, absent matches and teleports reject history. External module ABIs remain unchanged. A reused ID with no supplied spawn generation cannot universally distinguish a respawn.

audit.finding: Frequently read uploads use host memory without a VRAM preference.
audit.disposition: Material, stage, light and dynamic uploads prefer coherent host-visible device-local memory, retaining portable allocation fallback. Heap/type/flags are logged. The latched diagnostic `rtx_rt_device_local` permits A/B. The probe confirms different selected heaps; varying GPU contention prevents an isolated speedup claim.

audit.finding: Missing indirect samples and reused light choices need explicit treatment.
audit.disposition: Indirect validity and history are independent of direct light. Missing samples are not black observations. Weighted proposals improve light selection. Optional common-random-number replay shares four rotating candidate streams across compatible primary receivers; current PDFs, selection and visibility are always evaluated. Energy and current-visibility tests pass. Runtime noise did not improve, so `rtx_rt_light_reuse` remains **0 by default**. This is not ReSTIR reservoir reuse.

audit.finding: Full-resolution tracing and large intermediates dominate cost.
audit.disposition: Independent indirect divisors 1–4, rotating coverage phases, depth/normal-guided reconstruction and an optional GPU budget reduce bounce work while preserving full-rate primary/direct work. Depth/normal and motion use RG32UI; moments store mean/stddev in RGBA16F. Shared variance work is computed once. The 25 intermediate images total 192 bytes/pixel, 180 MiB at 720p. Their storage remains full resolution.

audit.finding: A cell's 64-light cap removes other emitters from sampling.
audit.disposition: Overflow cells, omitted entries and importance are counted. The global proposal has power weighting with a 10% uniform floor and participates in the exact local/global mixture PDF, including MIS replacement. Every light retains support. Sorted retained IDs make membership a binary search. Executed Monte Carlo tests cross disjoint cell lists and omitted lights, with and without reuse and changing visibility.

audit.finding: `RF_NOSHADOW` is not a separate ray visibility policy.
audit.disposition: Internal vertex metadata excludes flagged entities only from shadow visibility; primary/reflected geometry remains. Hardware uses a shadow-specific any-hit SBT group. BODY is excluded from primary rays but remains a shadow caster unless flagged. Software/hardware tests and captures show the shadow disappearing with the flag.
